goal: Add a nullable blocked_requires_json column to the lifecycles row (SQLite + Postgres schemas, Lifecycle dataclass, and all store INSERT/UPDATE/SELECT paths) that round-trips through every backend.

references: src/flywheel/lifecycle.py:86-98 -- Lifecycle dataclass: add blocked_requires_json: str | None = None as a new nullable field, default None

src/flywheel/_schema/persistence-schema.sql:18-31 -- lifecycles CREATE TABLE that gains a `blocked_requires_json TEXT` column (nullable, no DEFAULT clause needed because TEXT NULL is the SQLite default)
src/flywheel/store_sqlite.py:158-228 -- INSERT and UPDATE statements for lifecycles, plus the SELECT projection at line 243+; round-trip the new column
src/flywheel/store_postgres.py:214-308 -- mirror the same change for the Postgres CREATE TABLE, INSERT, UPDATE, and SELECT
src/flywheel/store_memory.py -- in-memory store must preserve the new field across create_lifecycle / update_lifecycle / load_lifecycle
constraints: The new column is `blocked_requires_json TEXT` (nullable) in SQLite and `blocked_requires_json TEXT` (nullable) in Postgres. No CHECK constraint, no index, no DEFAULT clause -- NULL is the default. Mirror the same column-name spelling in both schemas exactly.

Lifecycle gains `blocked_requires_json: str | None = None`. The harness owns serialization/deserialization; this module stores the value verbatim. Do NOT import json into flywheel.lifecycle -- the existing purity test (tests/test_lifecycle_module_purity.py) must continue to pass unchanged.

All three stores (SqliteStore, PostgresStore, InMemoryStore) must round-trip the value: create_lifecycle persists it, update_lifecycle updates it (including setting it back to NULL), load_lifecycle returns it, and list/by-task queries that surface Lifecycle objects populate it. A SELECT * projection alone is not enough -- explicitly include the column in any hand-written SELECT lists.

Round-trip tests in tests/test_store_sqlite.py, tests/test_store_postgres.py, and tests/test_store_memory.py: persist a Lifecycle with blocked_requires_json set to a non-empty JSON string, reload, assert equality; persist a Lifecycle with blocked_requires_json=None, reload, assert it stays None; update an existing row from a non-None value back to None, reload, assert clearing worked.
Extend tests/test_store_contract.py (the shared contract test) so the round-trip assertion runs against every backend uniformly -- this prevents one store from drifting.
Do NOT add migration scripts. New columns on existing rows are NULL by default; the spec explicitly accepts this back-compat path (Non-Functional Requirements: Schema migration).
Do NOT add any harness or workflow logic in this task. The harness wiring (populating the column on block, clearing on -> READY) lives in the next task.
Run `mcp__ide__getDiagnostics` on every .py file you touch and fix all Pylance errors before reporting verify.
Commit the change with a Conventional Commits message (e.g. 'feat:' or 'refactor:') before reporting verify.
non_goals: Do not import json into flywheel.lifecycle; do not add helpers that parse the column. Serialization is the harness's job.
Do not change any other column on lifecycles or any other table.
Do not change the Lifecycle.transition_to logic in this task -- clearing on -> READY belongs to the harness task.
Do not edit docs in this task; documentation updates ride with the harness task that defines the behavior.
edge_cases: The Postgres store may need its CREATE TABLE column-list order to match the SQLite one for symmetry, but does not strictly require it. Match the visual order to make diffs reviewable.
load_lifecycle must default the field to None when the stored value is SQL NULL -- do not coerce NULL to empty string.
If any store implements a copy / clone path for Lifecycle, make sure blocked_requires_json is propagated.
